data.title: Auto-escalate requests for configured safety-critical equipment to Critical

criteria.given: no `app.safety.critical-equipment-ids` configured (property absent, or `new WorkRequestSorter()` / `new WorkRequestProcessor(validator, resolver, sorter)` used directly)
criteria.then: no request's priority changes, no `SAFETY_ESCALATION` problem is produced, and the prioritize stage's queue, problems and trace are byte-for-byte what they are today (the 13-request sample batch still yields its pinned queue, problems and trace counts 13 → 10 → 6)

criteria.given: `application.yml` / a Spring environment
criteria.then: it is a record `SafetyProperties(@ConfigurationProperties("app.safety")` prefix) with a single component `List<String> criticalEquipmentIds` bound from `app.safety.critical-equipment-ids`, defaulting to an empty immutable list when the key is absent; the accessor never returns null; null and blank entries in the configured list are ignored; duplicate entries have no extra effect

criteria.given: `app.safety.critical-equipment-ids` contains `PUMP-7`, and a valid request `REQ-1` for `equipmentId` `PUMP-7` with priority `LOW` at input index 3
criteria.then: the queued `WorkRequest` for `REQ-1` has priority `CRITICAL` (built via `withPriority`), and exactly one `Problem` is returned with `inputIndex` 3, `requestId` `REQ-1`, `code` `ProblemCode.SAFETY_ESCALATION`, `escalatedFrom` `LOW`, `escalatedTo` `CRITICAL`, `field` null, `relatedRequestId` null, and `message` exactly `REQ-1 escalated LOW to CRITICAL because equipment PUMP-7 is safety-critical`

criteria.given: the `Problem` domain record
criteria.when: `Problem.safetyEscalation(int inputIndex, String requestId, String equipmentId, Priority escalatedFrom)` is called
criteria.then: it returns a problem with `code` `SAFETY_ESCALATION`, `escalatedTo` always `Priority.CRITICAL`, `escalatedFrom` as passed, `field` and `relatedRequestId` null, and the message format `<requestId> escalated <escalatedFrom> to CRITICAL because equipment <equipmentId> is safety-critical`; `ProblemCode` gains the constant `SAFETY_ESCALATION` as its last constant, leaving the existing constants and their order unchanged

criteria.given: `PUMP-7` is configured safety-critical and request `REQ-9` for `PUMP-7` already has priority `CRITICAL`
criteria.then: `REQ-9` stays `CRITICAL`, no `SAFETY_ESCALATION` problem is produced for it, and no escalation note mentions it (escalation only applies when the current priority weight is below `CRITICAL.weight()`)

criteria.given: `PUMP-7` is configured safety-critical and a valid `LOW` request for `equipmentId` `CONVEYOR-2`
criteria.then: that request keeps priority `LOW` and produces no `SAFETY_ESCALATION` problem

criteria.given: `app.safety.critical-equipment-ids` contains `  pump-7 ` (mixed case, surrounding whitespace) and a `MEDIUM` request whose `equipmentId` is `PUMP-7`
criteria.then: the request is escalated to `CRITICAL`; matching trims and ignores ASCII case on both the configured ids and the request's `equipmentId`, and the message quotes the request's own `equipmentId` value as submitted (`PUMP-7`), not the configured spelling

criteria.given: `PUMP-7` is safety-critical and two duplicate requests for `PUMP-7` (kept `REQ-1` at `LOW`, duplicate `REQ-2` at `HIGH`) in one batch
criteria.then: escalation runs after deduplication and before sorting: `REQ-1` is first raised to `HIGH` by the duplicate rule, then to `CRITICAL` by safety escalation, so the returned problems are the `DUPLICATE` problem for `REQ-2` (escalatedFrom `LOW`, escalatedTo `HIGH`) followed by a `SAFETY_ESCALATION` problem for `REQ-1` with `escalatedFrom` `HIGH` and `escalatedTo` `CRITICAL`, and the queued `REQ-1` is `CRITICAL`

criteria.given: a request for safety-critical equipment that is missing `description` (or has an invalid `priority`)
criteria.then: validation still runs first: the request is rejected with its `MISSING_FIELD` / `INVALID_VALUE` problems only, it never reaches escalation, no `SAFETY_ESCALATION` problem is produced for it, and it is not in the queue

criteria.given: a batch containing escalated and non-escalated requests
criteria.when: the same batch is processed in 100 shuffled orders
criteria.then: the queue, the full problem list and the trace are identical every time; escalated requests sort with `CRITICAL.weight()` (so above `HIGH` requests), ties broken by `requestedAt` ascending then `requestId` ascending, and within the prioritize stage the `SAFETY_ESCALATION` problems are ordered by ascending `inputIndex`

criteria.given: a batch in which two requests are escalated
criteria.then: the trace still has exactly three entries `validate`, `deduplicate`, `prioritize`; the `prioritize` entry's `in` and `out` both equal the number of requests reaching that stage (escalation drops nothing), and its `notes` contain one note per escalated request equal to that request's `SAFETY_ESCALATION` problem message, sorted in natural order and free of input indices

criteria.given: the processing classes
criteria.then: a new framework-free class `SafetyEscalator` exists with constructors `SafetyEscalator(java.util.Collection<String> criticalEquipmentIds)` and `SafetyEscalator(SafetyProperties properties)` and a method `StageResult escalate(List<IndexedRequest> requests)` returning the escalated requests (input order preserved), the `SAFETY_ESCALATION` problems ordered by `inputIndex`, and a `StageTrace` with stage name `prioritize`, `in` == `out` == `requests.size()` and the sorted escalation notes; `WorkRequestSorter` gains a `WorkRequestSorter(SafetyEscalator)` constructor used by `sort`, while the existing no-arg `WorkRequestSorter()` keeps working by defaulting to an escalator with no configured ids

criteria.given: the Spring context
criteria.then: `ProcessingConfig` declares a `SafetyEscalator` bean built from the `SafetyProperties` bean and passes it to the `WorkRequestSorter` bean; `SafetyProperties` is picked up by the existing `@ConfigurationPropertiesScan`; no `@Component` annotations are added to main code; a context started without `app.safety.*` set still starts and escalates nothing

criteria.given: a POST of a batch containing one request for configured safety-critical equipment at `LOW`
criteria.then: the queued request's `priority` is `CRITICAL` and the response contains a problem whose `code` is `SAFETY_ESCALATION` with `escalatedFrom` `LOW`, `escalatedTo` `CRITICAL` and the explanatory message, so the escalation reason is visible without parsing free text beyond the equipment id

criteria.given: `BatchObserver` metrics and the generated order-independence batch
criteria.when: a batch containing a safety escalation is observed
criteria.then: `BatchObserver` records a counter for `ProblemCode.SAFETY_ESCALATION` using the same naming scheme as the existing per-code counters (one counter per `ProblemCode` value, including the new one), and the generated batch used by `OrderIndependenceTest.generatedBatchCoversEveryKindOfProblem` includes a request on configured safety-critical equipment so that every `ProblemCode` value, `SAFETY_ESCALATION` included, is produced

outOfScope: Matching by wildcard, regex, equipment class/type or hierarchy — only exact (trimmed, case-insensitive) equipment id matches
Reloading the safety-critical list at runtime; the list is read at startup from configuration
De-escalation or capping: nothing ever lowers a priority, and escalation only ever targets CRITICAL
Adding a fourth pipeline stage or changing the trace to anything other than validate/deduplicate/prioritize
Changing deduplication, validation or sorting rules themselves
Introducing a java.time.Clock bean or any time-based escalation (staleness, SLA)
Persisting escalations, notifications, or audit logging beyond the returned problem and trace note
Populating sample-batch.json or application.yml with real safety-critical ids (default stays empty so pinned sample-batch expectations hold)
Frontend/UI changes and any authorisation rules around who may escalate
